sentences.text: This appeal by the appellant/claimant u/S. 173 (1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is arising out of the award dated 26.02.2020 passed by 5th Additional MACT, Morena (M.P.) (in short "Claims Tribunal") in Claim Case No.23/2018 on account of inadequacy of compensation and seeking enhancement of compensation.
2. Brief facts of the case are that on 28.03.2017, claimant Jagdish Singh was going to Bareta from his house on a motorbike.
His son Sudhir was sitting behind him on the motorcycle.
Jagdish was driving his motorcycle carefully and reached Shanichara Road situated within the vicinity area of Police Station Rithorakalan, Morena.

Meanwhile, the Driver of Maruti Van bearing No.MP 06 BA 0895 came from the wrong side and drove it in rash and negligent manner and hit the motorcycle of the Jagdish as a result of which, he suffered serious injury in the spinal cord and his spinal cord got fractured and some part of the spinal cord got compressed and some bones got displaced
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:20670 2 MA-2022-2020 from their place and the nerves and veins of the spinal cord got destroyed, therefore, he suffered permanent disability to the tune of 100%.
Thereafter, alleged incident was reported to Police Station and they registered FIR at Crime No.33/2017.
After investigation, charge-sheet was filed before the Competent Court.
3. Thereafter, claimant/imjured filed claim petition for seeking compensation before the Tribunal.

sentences.text: 4. After hearing both the parties, Claims Tribunal framed issues and after taking evidence of both the parties, awarded compensation in favour of claimant to the tune of Rs.16,15,600/- with interest from the date of filing of claim application till its realization.
5. Being aggrieved by the impugned award, claimant/appellant/injured filed this appeal on the ground that Claims Tribunal has awarded the compensation is on lower side.

It is further submitted that he is a Manufacturer of the trolley, thresher and other agricultural equipment of which,
Registration Certificate is Ex.P-191-C, therefore, his income must be assessed to the tune of Rs.20,000/- per month.
It is further submitted that Claims Tribunal has also committed an error in not awarding any future prospects in favour of claimant.

Compensation must be assessed by Claims Tribunal on the basis of permanent disability by adding proper future prospect, multiplier,
treatment expenses, special diet and loss of income, mental agony, future treatment, attendant charge, transportation expenses and other heads etc.
6.

On the other hand, learned counsel for the Insurance Company NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:20670 3 MA-2022-2020 contended that the Claims Tribunal has rightly awarded the compensation and argued in support of the findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal.
The Insurance Company filed a cross-objection under Order 41 Rule 22 CPC r/w 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act stating that the injuries sustained by claimant himself is due to the accident by bike.
Hence, prayed for setting aside the impugned award.
7. In reply, learned counsel for the claimant prayed for rejection of cross-objection.

8. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and on perusal of the entire record as well as impugned award, it appears that in cross-objection the Insurance Company submitted that according to Ex.D-2 (Discharge summary) issued by Dr.Anoop Kr Kaushik, claimant injured suffered injuries due to the accident by bike, but the said Doctor was not examined by the Insurance Company before Claims Tribunal.

So, lack of evidence of Dr.Anoop Kr Kaushik, this fact was not duly proved and considering the findings giving by Claims Tribunal in paras 11, 12, 13 and 14 its impugned award, this Court is of the view that Claims Tribunal after marshalling the evidence on record has rightly held that the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Driver of the offending vehicle.
Therefore, cross- objection filed by Insurance Company has no substance.
9. So far as the income of deceased is concerned, in the present case, appellant was unable to adduce any documentary evidence before the Claims Tribunal to prove his income.

Claimant has failed to produce any income tax return or any passbook to prove that how much amount was deposited by NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:20670 4 MA-2022-2020 him regarding income tax as well as sales tax.

Due to lack of such evidence, the Claims Tribunal has rightly assessed income of the deceased @ Rs.6,950/- per month which is just and and, therefore, there is no need to interfere of this Court in this regard.

10. As regards loss of income including future prospects, in the light of judgment of National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi , 2017 ACJ 2700, the claimant is entitled for future prospects of 10% as he was 60 years old at the time of alleged accident.

Further, as per the judgment of the Apex Jagdeesh Singh vs Hakim Singh on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153099785/
2 Court in the case of Sarla Verma and ors. Vs Delhi Transport Corporation and Anr. reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121 , even if age of the injured is to be taken into account, then multiplier of 9 has rightly been applied by Claims Tribunal.

sentences.text: Further, considering the injuries sustained by claimant in the alleged accident and medical evidence, this Court thinks appropriate that an additional amount of Rs.1,25,000/- must be enhanced towards other heads.

11. Accordingly, appellants are entitled to get compensation under the following heads:-
 Heads Amount  Income Rs,6  Rs.6  Annual Income  8340  After adding Future Prospect 10% Rs.9  Multiplier 9 Rs.8  Medical Bill Rs.5

Other Heads (physical and mental agony, transportation, Rs.4,10,000/-
attendant charge, special diet, future treatment etc.) Total Rs.18,15,660/-
12.

Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the instant NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:20670 5 MA-2022-2020 case is Rs,18,15,660/- as against the Award of the Claims Tribunal o f Rs.16,15,600/-.
Accordingly, the appellants/claimants are entitled to an additional sum of Rs.2,00,060/- over and above the amount, which has been awarded by the Claims Tribunal.
13. In the result, this miscellaneous appeal is partly allowed, by enhancing the compensation amount by a sum of Rs.2,00,060/-.
The enhanced amount shall carry interest as fixed by the learned Claims Tribunal from the date of filing of claim petition till its realization.
The said amount be paid within a period of three months from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
Rest of conditions as imposed by learned Claims Tribunal shall remain intact.

14. If the enhanced amount of compensation is in excess to the valuation of appeal, the difference of the Court fee (if not already paid) shall be deposited by the appellants within a period of one month and proof thereof, shall be submitted before the Registry.
Thereafter, the Registry shall issue the certified copy of the order passed today.
15. In view of above, miscellaneous appeal filed by the appellants stands disposed of.

(HIRDESH) JUDGE *AVI*
